Empagliflozin in adults with heart failure

In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome both trials register as their primary?

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. That agreement is not the main uncertainty here. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event and this pool combines odds ratios computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but read the pooled number as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as published0.7576 (0.6825 to 0.8409)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.7576 (0.385 to 1.4907)

The published point is 0.7576 and the house-rule point is 0.7576. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives. And both intervals in this table bracket an odds ratio computed over unequal follow-up. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event; this pool combines odds ratios from cumulative arm counts over trials of different duration, and an odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled. Which of these two interval methods is preferred is a smaller question than which quantity is being bracketed.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

The bound on this claimIt is 'no identified synthesis', never 'no synthesis'. The screen matched 130 records, retrieved 25, appraised 5 and did not read 125. What is not establishedThe allocation concealment mechanism is not described in the registration, and the methods section that would describe it is not open access. LOW is scored on randomisation and balance; it is not scored on a concealment mechanism nobody here has read.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred ; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes no information on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at some concerns. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at some concerns or HIGH by another no information domain.
Named by hand because its evidence is weaker stillthe randomisation process was scored LOW citing the registered title containing the word randomised, plus balanced arm sizes. The design module is not cited. A title adjective is the thinnest possible form of the situation the guidance names.
And this one also inferred concealment from arm balanceThis judgement cited, in addition, that the arm sizes are balanced and that this is what a concealed sequence produces. That is an inference, not a registry fact. Balanced arms are consistent with concealment and do not establish it, and RoB 2 signalling question 1.3 asks whether baseline differences suggest a problem -- a different question from whether concealment was adequate. The entry states in its own words that the mechanism was never read.
Read from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-21. The judgements above were not revisited -- this adds the registry evidence beside a verdict that was made from it and did not record it, so a blind second assessor can be shown the same facts. A second assessment built on fewer facts is not a comparable assessment.
Named by hand because its evidence is weaker stillAs NCT03057977 -- the same two trials on the same object, judged from the same registered title wording.
The allow list the rate is conditional onA disagreement rate is meaningless without the facts both assessors saw, so the list is stated here the way a denominator is stated. Fields emitted: trial, cohort, registered enrolment, registered masking, registered sites, registered comparator, number of registered arms, number of registered primary outcomes, registered primary outcome, registered analysis population, the rank the pooled result holds, the result being assessed, participants this review pools, registered enrolment minus participants pooled. Established by test, not argument: widening this list from 9 fields to 14 halved gepotidacin's disagreement -- its entire selection of the reported result divergence was a fact the second assessor had never been shown -- and left ceftaroline and tigecycline unmoved.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Empagliflozin in adults with heart failure1

A claim on this object is withdrawn as false. It asserted that no published synthesis pools this review's two trials. Emperor-pooled is exactly that: a prospectively planned pooled analysis of EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved, at individual-patient level, with multiple indexed publications. It is not an obscure record and it is not a near-match; it is a pooled analysis of precisely the two trials, designed as one before either reported. The claim is withdrawn and not deleted. What it said, that it was false, and what is true are all recorded here, because a claim that quietly disappears cannot be audited and a reader who acted on it has no way to learn that it was wrong. What this means for the comparison: the published-synthesis comparison on this object was drawn against a stated absence that does not exist. It should be re-run against EMPEROR-Pooled. That is work, not a correction, and it is not done here.2

Results

The pooled odds ratio for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) was 0.758 (0.682 to 0.841) across 2 trials, against placebo.1

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.369, on degrees of freedom 1. Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. That agreement is not the main uncertainty here. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event and this pool combines odds ratios computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. An odds ratio over unequal follow-up is not a hazard ratio and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but read the pooled number as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.2

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.3

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.4

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/empagliflozin-hf-auto-full-review/appraisal/the screen of published syntheses.json. 130 records matched, 25 retrieved, 5 appraised, 125 not read. Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1
